title: The potential impact of exercise on affect and neuroinflammation in older adults living with fibromyalgia: a scoping review
authors: Taylor L. Taylor; Fitzgerald Dodds; McKenna Tharpe; Emily L. Zumbro; Michael Hankes; Raymond Jones; Deanna Rumble; Lisa Antoine; Kristen Allen-Watts; Andrew Sims; Reshu Chandra; Burel R. Goodin; Jarred Younger; Thomas W. Buford
pain_condition_detail: Fibromyalgia (FM), a widespread chronic pain condition, in older adults aged 65 years or older.
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses the Biopsychosocial Framework of Chronic Pain as an organizing principle to structure the review around affect (psychological) and neuroinflammation (biological), but does not define the model or integrate social factors substantively. The framework is invoked in the abstract and conclusion but not operationalized in methods or results.
integration_mechanism_summary: None proposed. The paper asserts directional relationships between exercise and affect, and between neuroinflammation and affect, but does not specify pathways or mediators. Social factors are mentioned as benefits of exercise but not integrated with biological or psychological domains.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper claims a biopsychosocial framework but focuses almost exclusively on biological (neuroinflammation) and psychological (affect) domains, with social factors only mentioned in passing
conceptual_tensions_2: The relationship between neuroinflammation and affect is asserted as directional but no mechanism or mediator is specified, leaving the integration claim weak
conceptual_tensions_3: Exercise adherence is discussed as an outcome but the review does not systematically examine how biological or psychological factors causally influence adherence
additional_observations_1: The paper proposes a conceptual framework in a figure (not provided in text) illustrating reciprocal relationships between exercise, affective changes, neuroinflammation, and exercise adherence, but the text does not elaborate on the mechanisms
additional_observations_2: The review includes quality assessment using Cochrane risk of bias tool but does not weight study conclusions by quality, which is appropriate for a scoping review
synthesis_note: This scoping review uses the biopsychosocial label to frame a review of exercise effects on affect and neuroinflammation in older adults with fibromyalgia, but operationalizes only two domains (psychological and biological) with minimal social content. Integration is directional at best, with no specified mechanisms. The paper contributes a conceptual framework but does not test or define it.
coding_rationale: Typology is pseudo_bps because BPS language is used but social domain is minimal and integration is absent. Triadic integration is none because social domain is not integrated. Psych-dominant because affect outcomes are elaborated while biological and social are thin.

pain_condition_detail: Fibromyalgia (FM); eligibility allowed FM-related Chronic Fatigue Syndrome, but extracted study characteristics state all studies evaluated exercise in FM samples.
context_note: NIA Health Disparities Framework highlights geographic/political factors, cultural factors, coping factors, and physiological indicators as pain research priorities.
bps_function_set: background framing; intervention rationale; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper operationalizes BPS as exercise plus affect and neuroinflammation outcomes, with adherence and social barriers as context; it does not define the model or assign coded variables to all three domains.
integration_mechanism_summary: Proposed pathway: exercise changes affect and inflammatory/neuroinflammatory markers; cytokines/microglia/BBB link inflammation to dysregulated affect and pain; affect changes and neuroinflammation may improve adherence. Social factors are barriers/context, not part of the pathway.
conceptual_tensions_1: The review proposes neuroinflammation/affect mechanisms while stating evidence is limited and attribution speculative
conceptual_tensions_2: Exercise is framed as beneficial, yet acute bouts can worsen pain/fatigue and drive fear avoidance/adherence problems
conceptual_tensions_3: The review focuses on older adults but notes many included participants were young and middle-aged adults
conceptual_tensions_4: Social factors are invoked through barriers and disparities but are not measured or integrated into the main mechanism
conceptual_tensions_5: Scoping review methods included all available literature and did not weight conclusions by quality despite risk-of-bias assessments
additional_observations_1: No named psychological or social instruments are used, outcomes are reported as study outcomes
additional_observations_2: The conceptual framework is central but is proposed for future testing rather than tested in this review
additional_observations_3: The paper treats exercise as both lifestyle behavior and intervention component
additional_observations_4: It distinguishes neuroinflammation from systemic inflammation but uses both in mechanisms
additional_observations_5: It calls for qualitative approaches to exercise adherence
additional_observations_6: Quality assessments were conducted but not weighted in the scoping review synthesis
synthesis_note: The review operationalizes BPS mainly through exercise, affect, neuroinflammation, and adherence in older adults with FM. It develops biological and psychological mechanisms while social factors remain barriers/context, yielding partial BPS integration.
coding_rationale: Bio and psych are elaborated; social is thin. BPS label organizes the review and supports exercise rationale, but no model definition or full triadic integration is provided.

authors: Taylor L. Taylor; Fitzgerald Dodds; McKenna Tharpe; Emily L. Zumbro; Michael Hankes; Raymond Jones; Deanna Rumble; Lisa Antoine; Kristen Allen-Watts; Andrew Sims; Reshu Chandra; Burel R. Goodin; Jarred Younger; Thomas W. Buford
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The review uses BPS as an organizing framework to structure its investigation of exercise effects on affect and neuroinflammation in fibromyalgia, but does not integrate the three domains through specified mechanisms or pathways.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes directional relationships: exercise improves affect and may reduce neuroinflammation; neuroinflammation contributes to depression; fear avoidance and depression create barriers to exercise adherence. A conceptual framework suggests reciprocal relationships between these factors, but no detailed mechanistic pathways are specified.
conceptual_tensions_1: Tension between the BPS framework's promise of integration and the paper's limited empirical evidence for biological outcomes
conceptual_tensions_2: Gap between the conceptual framework's reciprocal relationships and the lack of detailed mechanistic pathways
conceptual_tensions_3: Mismatch between the BPS label and the actual depth of social domain content
additional_observations_1: The review focuses on older adults with fibromyalgia, a specific population within chronic pain
additional_observations_2: Exercise modalities studied include aerobic, resistance, combined, and stretching exercises
additional_observations_3: Quality assessment was conducted but studies were not weighted in conclusions
additional_observations_4: The review acknowledges its own limitations in participant demographics and outcome measurement
synthesis_note: This scoping review operationalizes the biopsychosocial model as an organizing framework to investigate exercise effects on affect and neuroinflammation in older adults with fibromyalgia. While the psychological domain is well-developed with constructs like affective styles and depression, biological content is limited to theoretical mechanisms with sparse empirical evidence. Social domain content is minimal. The review proposes a conceptual framework suggesting reciprocal relationships but lacks detailed mechanistic integration. The BPS label serves primarily as an organizing principle rather than an explanatory framework with specified pathways.
coding_rationale: BPS typology as 'multifactorial' because all three domains are present but not mechanistically integrated. Triadic integration as 'partial' due to conceptual framework suggesting relationships but lacking detailed pathways. Psychological domain scored 'elaborated' due to multiple named constructs and their relationships.
